content: Participants in the survey have the option to consent to the storage of their blood samples for future testing that may be deemed relevant to public health by the Ministry of Health. This consent is entirely voluntary. Since the samples will be anonymized at the conclusion of the study, meaning the link between the participant and their unique identifier will be severed, the results of any future testing cannot be shared with the participant. The survey aims to identify individuals with hepatitis B (HBV) or hepatitis C (HCV) infections, who will then be referred for appropriate medical care. If a statistical sampling method is used, the survey will provide reliable, population-based estimates of the prevalence of viral hepatitis biomarkers. These estimates will help assess the country’s progress toward achieving regional and global goals for controlling or eliminating hepatitis. Additionally, the data will serve as input for modeling efforts to estimate the current burden of infection and evaluate various prevention, testing, and treatment strategies, such as vaccination, infection control, and medical care. The roles and responsibilities of all participating institutions will be clearly outlined, including the names and contact details of key personnel. A written report summarizing the survey findings will be prepared within four months of completing the testing phase. The principal investigator will also prepare a manuscript for submission to a peer-reviewed journal, with authorship determined based on international criteria and individual contributions. The survey will follow a predefined timeline, which includes planning all associated procedures and scheduling sessions with the ethics committee in advance. The budget for the survey will adhere to the estimates provided in the relevant template. Participants will be informed about the purpose of the survey, which is to assess the prevalence of hepatitis B and C in the country. They will be asked to answer a few questions and provide a blood sample for testing. Participation is entirely voluntary, and individuals can withdraw at any time without providing a reason. Refusal to participate will not affect their access to healthcare services. The survey will take approximately a specified amount of time, during which participants will answer questions about their health history and risk factors, and a small blood sample will be collected for testing. The risks associated with the survey are minimal but may include discomfort, bruising, or swelling at the blood draw site, and in rare cases, fainting or infection. If any issues arise as a result of the study, participants will receive appropriate treatment at no cost. Participants will also have access to their test results within a specified timeframe. Any leftover blood samples after testing will be destroyed. Participation in the survey will contribute significantly to public health efforts in the country, and participants will benefit from knowing their hepatitis status. Those who test positive will be referred to appropriate treatment facilities and supported throughout the process. Confidentiality will be strictly maintained. Data collected will only be accessible to the implementing institution and its partners, and participants’ names will not appear on any records. Instead, unique identifiers will be used. Survey results will be presented or published without referencing participants’ names, and all records will be securely stored. Participants have the right to stop participating at any time without penalty. They may also refuse to answer specific questions or withdraw from the survey entirely, without affecting their access to healthcare services. Contact information for the principal investigator and the ethics committee will be provided for any questions or concerns about the study or its ethical aspects. Participants will be asked to sign a consent form, which will not waive any of their legal rights. A copy of the signed consent form will be provided to them for their records. For children, assent will also be obtained, and a literate witness may be required to sign if the child is illiterate.
